summary.headline: Costco presented wetland and stormwater plans for a proposed 167,000-square-foot warehouse and gas station on Coslin Drive.
summary.summary: The Southborough Conservation Commission reviewed initial stormwater and wetlands plans for a proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco warehouse and 30-position fueling station at 21 Coslin Drive. The commission also voted to recommend town resident Rajesh Bhutani for appointment to the board and heard a presentation on a volunteer native planting project at Beals Preserve. Multiple public hearings were continued to November 19, including applications for a septic system replacement at Stonebrook Village, Fay School athletic turf fields, and a 32-unit townhouse development on Turnpike Road.

topics.title: Conservation Commission applicant interview: Rajesh Bhutani
topics.summary: The commission interviewed Middle Road resident Rajesh Bhutani for an open seat on the board. Bhutani, a retired corporate CPA and MBA who has lived in Southborough for 22 years, discussed his background, community walking habits, and approach to consensus-building. The commission voted unanimously to recommend his appointment to the Select Board.
key_details: Applicant Rajesh Bhutani has resided on Middle Road in Southborough for 22 years.
Bhutani brings a professional background as a CPA and MBA in corporate business.
Commission members emphasized their collaborative track record with applicants while upholding state and local wetland bylaws.
topics.outcome: Voted 4-0 to recommend Rajesh Bhutani to the Select Board for appointment.

topics.title: Beals Preserve native plant buffer project
topics.summary: Algonquin Regional High School senior Lily Spezzano presented a multi-year volunteer project coordinated with the Southborough Open Land Foundation at Beals Preserve off Red Gate Lane. Based on forester recommendations, the project installs native shrubs around an ice pond to provide wildlife habitat, food, and cover. Ten shrubs were planted in late October with additional volunteer planting scheduled for early November.
key_details: Project site is located around the ice pond and wetland at Beals Preserve on Red Gate Lane.
Recommended by forester Tom Ashton to create a 300-meter native shrub buffer around a tree stand.
Shrub species selected include winterberry, American hazelnut, silky dogwood, and swamp azalea.
Volunteers planted 10 shrubs in late October, with 10 to 12 more scheduled for the first weekend of November.

topics.title: Notice of Intent: Woodland Road Town Forest footbridge
topics.summary: The commission opened a public hearing on a Notice of Intent for Map 22, Lots 3A and 8 in the Town Forest to remove and replace an existing footbridge. Because abutter notifications were not completed prior to the meeting, no discussion occurred.
key_details: Applicant is Kaylee Theisen for project located in the Town Forest.
Hearing could not proceed due to missing abutter notification.

topics.title: Notice of Intent: Stonebrook Village septic system replacement
topics.summary: Engineer Scott Peoples presented plans on behalf of Salisbury Management LLC to replace a failed Presby soil absorption system serving condominium units at Stonebrook Village on Map 15, Lot 16. The project requires excavating the failed field, removing improper fill and stone dust down to Title 5 sand, and trucking in new specified sand while daily pumping ensures wastewater does not overflow near adjacent wetlands.
key_details: Property is located at Stonebrook Village off Woodland and Oregon roads.
The failed Presby leaching field is designed for 2,250 gallons per day, with current actual usage around 1,000 gallons per day.
Test pits revealed improper loam, roots, large rocks, and stone dust around the pipes rather than required Title 5 concrete sand.
Curtis Septic will pump the 7,000-gallon septic tank and pump chamber during the estimated two-week reconstruction.
topics.outcome: Continued to November 19, 2026, pending receipt of a DEP file number.

topics.title: Notice of Intent and Stormwater Permit: Costco Wholesale at 21 Coslin Drive
topics.summary: Representatives from BL Companies and legal counsel presented wetlands and stormwater permit applications for a proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco warehouse and 30-position gas fueling station on a 22-acre site at 21 Coslin Drive straddling Southborough and Westborough. The project replaces the demolished former Dell EMC office building and introduces comprehensive stormwater treatment systems, including deep-sump catch basins, hydrodynamic separators, and two constructed stormwater wetland basins. Peer reviewer Lucas Environmental submitted disclosure forms noting prior private work for Costco outside Southborough, and the commission chair disclosed employment with Dell Technologies.
key_details: Site comprises 22 total acres at 21 Coslin Drive, with 17.8 acres in Southborough and 8.3 acres in Westborough.
Proposed construction includes a 167,000-square-foot retail warehouse, a 30-position gas station with 15 pumps, and 895 parking spaces.
Stormwater plan includes two constructed wetland detention basins with sediment forebays and an oil-water separator at the fueling station.
Work in the 100-foot buffer zone includes milling Coslin Drive, removing existing pavement, and adding street trees and landscape plantings.
Lucas Environmental submitted a disclosure regarding prior work for Costco outside Southborough, and commissioners raised no objections to their continued peer review.
topics.outcome: Continued to November 19, 2026, pending consultant peer review and DEP comments.
topics.why_it_matters: The massive commercial redevelopment will replace a vacant office parcel on Route 9 with a major retail warehouse and gas facility, altering local traffic patterns and managing large-scale stormwater runoff near protected wetlands.

topics.title: Continued hearings: Fay School athletic fields and 250 Turnpike Road
topics.summary: The commission briefly opened and continued two ongoing hearings without substantive testimony. The New England Football Club proposal to reconstruct Fay School athletic fields from natural grass to artificial turf at 0 Marlboro Road was continued while wetland scientists review revisions. The proposed 32-townhouse project at 250 Turnpike Road was also continued at the applicant's request, prompting a commissioner request to place an item on the next agenda to address repeated meeting continuances.
key_details: 0 Marlboro Road involves turf field replacement for the New England Football Club at Fay School.
250 Turnpike Road involves a proposed 32-unit townhouse development.
A board member requested an agenda topic for the next meeting to discuss policy regarding repetitive project continuances.

topics.title: Certificates of Compliance: 12 Wood Street and Valley Road
topics.summary: The commission reviewed and unanimously approved Certificates of Compliance for completed projects at 12 Wood Street and on Valley Road. Work at 12 Wood Street completed house reconstruction and native buffer plantings, while the Valley Road project completed an Eagle Scout trail boardwalk and footbridge.
key_details: 12 Wood Street (DEP #290-1131): House rebuild, septic work, and required native shrub plantings are complete and stable.
Valley Road (DEP #290-1151): Completed an Eagle Scout footbridge and boardwalk built flush to natural terrain.

topics.title: Conservation Agent report: Beaver flooding, Valvoline, and road milling
topics.summary: The conservation agent updated the board on several ongoing town conservation matters. Madison Place management has hired a trapper to relocate beavers causing roadway flooding on Route 9 near 344 Turnpike Road. Additionally, Valvoline submitted a buffer restoration planting plan following improper clearing, Town Counsel is reviewing a draft land donation deed for 120 Turnpike Road, and erosion controls are being monitored during road milling along the Cordaville Road causeway.
key_details: Madison Place engaged a trapper to relocate beavers obstructing culverts and causing flooding near the Route 9 gas station.
Valvoline submitted a two-to-one native shrub and wetland restoration mix mitigation plan to resolve unauthorized buffer clearing.
Town Counsel is reviewing a draft land donation deed for 120 Turnpike Road.
Erosion control wattles are being monitored along the Cordaville Road causeway during DPW milling operations.
topics.outcome: Informational update; no formal votes taken.
